source_text:
8.2 Ἀφρικανοῦ ἐκ βίβλου γʹ Στῦψις δὲ πρὸς
πᾶσαν βαφὴν ἥδε· πρῶτα μὲν ἀποπλύνεται τὸ ζῷον ἢ καὶ νάκος· οὕτω γὰρ ἂν
πρόσοιτο τὰ τῆς στύψεως. Ἐπὶ δὲ τὴν στυπτηρίαν ἀναλυτέον ὄξει κἀπιχρίειν ὅπερ ἂν
βάψαι δέοι. Ἀφαυανθὲν δὲ ἡλίῳ ἀποπλύνεται καὶ τῆς νοτίδος ἐλευθερωθὲν πᾶσαν
προσίεται βαφήν. Νύκτα δὲ καὶ ἡμέραν ἐπὶ τῇ στύψει φυλάττειν χρὴ τὸ στυφόμενον.
pass_a_gloss: 8.2 Of-Africanus from book 3. Stypsis but toward every dyeing is-this: first yes is-washed-off the animal or also a-hide; thus for it-would-take-on the of-the-stypsis. Upon but the alum one-must-dissolve with-vinegar and-smear whatever one-would-dye. Having-been-dried but by-sun it-is-washed-off and of-the-moisture having-been-freed every dyeing it-takes-on. Night but and day upon the stypsis one-must-keep the being-stypticked.
pass_b_english: From Africanus, from book 3. Stypsis toward every dyeing is this: first the animal, or also the hide, is washed off; for thus it would take on the things of the stypsis. Then one must dissolve alum in vinegar and smear whatever one would dye. Dried in the sun it is washed off and, freed of the moisture, it takes on every dyeing. Night and day one must keep the thing being stypticked under the stypsis.

choices.english: Dried in the sun it is washed off
choices.why: ἀφαυαίνω is dry out, not 'appear in the sun'. The hide is dried, rinsed, then takes dye.
rejected: appearing in the sun it is washed

anf_compare.notes: No PD English of the Cesti body; ANF has the letters only.
